circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the Formula One calendar's final event since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern venue to join the F1 schedule, following Bahrain and preceding circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that winds around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds FIA Grade 1 classification. It serves as the permanent venue for the Australian Grand Prix and hosts various other motorsport events including the Supercars Championship round.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally operated as the Österreichring and held the Austrian Grand Prix annually throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following a reconstruction and renaming, the venue returned to hosting the Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along Baku Boulevard, and at 6. 003 km constitutes the fourth-longest venue in Formula One racing. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming home to the dedicated Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the championship's inaugural Middle Eastern event. The track holds a FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates various motorsport categories including drag racing, single-seater series, and endurance competitions, with multiple circuit configurations available.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced combination of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capabilities. The venue accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators and holds the FIA's highest safety certification.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The Belgian circuit at Francorchamps stretches over seven kilometers through the Walloon countryside near Spa and represents one of Formula One's most historic venues, having first hosted a Grand Prix in 1925 and participating in the championship's inaugural season in 1950. The track has maintained annual F1 races since 1985, with only brief interruptions in 2003 and 2006, making it the enduring home of the Belgian Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, this 4. 361 km street circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond Formula One, the venue has accommodated various international motorsport competitions, including World Sportscar Championship events and multiple North American racing series.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading district, this Chinese motorsport facility served as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix from 2004 until 2019, with the event returning from 2024. Beyond Formula One racing, the venue has also begun hosting electric racing competitions from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located in Northamptonshire, England, is the traditional home of the British Grand Prix, having staged the inaugural event in 1948 and the first-ever World Championship race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch between 1955 and 1986, the circuit became the permanent venue for Britain's Formula One race from 1987 onwards.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted Formula One's first Eastern Bloc Grand Prix in 1986, after Bernie Ecclestone sought a Soviet venue but settled on Hungary following a local recommendation. Built in just eight months near a major highway outside the city, the 4. 381 km circuit was constructed faster than any other Formula One track and held its inaugural race on 24 March 1986 in tribute to Hungarian motorcycle racing pioneer János Drapál.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 and ranks among the world's earliest purpose-built racing venues. The track has continuously hosted Formula One's Italian Grand Prix since 1949, except for a 1980 closure during renovation, making it one of the oldest fixtures on the championship calendar, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" from its characteristically long straightaways and fast-cornering design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, spans 5. 807 kilometers and is operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track accommodates 155,000 spectators and serves as a premier venue for both Formula One and Japanese Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street track that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding urban landscape. The layout passes by several of the city's most iconic venues, including major hotels, casinos, and landmarks like the Sphere, Caesars Palace, and Bellagio.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two Mexican racing brothers who tragically lost their lives in motorsport accidents during the 1960s. The venue has intermittently hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix, most recently as a continuous fixture since 2015 on its current configuration, after previous hosting periods that concluded in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that allows qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, the track became part of the championship calendar in 2022 and primarily hosts the Miami Grand Prix, though a modified version has been adapted for Formula E racing since the 2025-26 season.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, circling the principality's harbour. Though technically spanning two neighbourhoods, it is widely known as the Monte Carlo circuit due to its predominant location within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix starting in 2021 before the partnership concluded in 2026. The venue, situated north of the town of Zandvoort close to the North Sea, operated under various names throughout its history before adopting its current sponsored designation.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing venue positioned north of Doha near the city of Lusail, featuring a 5. 419 km track layout and a 1. 068 km main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in tribute to deceased Formula One driver José Carlos Pace. The venue hosts significant racing events and features additional facilities including a kart track dedicated to another Brazilian racing legend, Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront. Since 2021, it has served as the home of the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, and recently began hosting international electric racing competitions as well.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue located around Singapore's Marina Bay, incorporating areas from both Downtown Core and Kallang.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner types, making it a versatile test for all-around racing performance. The track holds an FIA Grade 1 license and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix alongside hosting major international motorsport events including MotoGP and the World Endurance Championship. The track has established itself as a premier racing venue by attracting diverse series ranging from NASCAR to sports car competitions throughout its operational history.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a driver of Thai and British nationality who races under Thailand's flag in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: The Spanish driver competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships during his tenure at Renault in 2005 and 2006, with 32 race victories accumulated over 23 seasons. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both the Formula One and World Endurance championships.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and has already secured eight Grand Prix victories while racing for Mercedes.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor who currently drives for Haas in Formula One racing.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for the Audi team. He represents the latest generation of South American talent competing at motorsport's highest level.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver competes for Cadillac in Formula One, having previously achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his tenure with Mercedes in 2019 and 2020. Over his 13-season career, he has secured 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Colapinto is an Argentine driver currently racing in Formula One for the Alpine team. He represents his nation in the sport's top competition.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while competing in prototype racing for Nielsen Racing in the European Le Mans Series. He made limited appearances in the sport's top category, participating in seven Grands Prix across the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The former AlphaTauri competitor achieved a remarkable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix, securing one of his most significant career results.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar represents France in Formula One, competing for Red Bull Racing. The Franco-Algerian driver brings dual nationality to his current role in the sport.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton, a British driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One. He has secured seven World Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record, while also holding the sport's all-time records for race victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg represents Germany in Formula One as an Audi driver. Beyond his current single-seater commitments, the accomplished racer secured victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche in endurance competition.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a racing driver from New Zealand, currently represents Racing Bulls in Formula One competition.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having secured a runner-up finish in the 2022 championship standings. Across his nine seasons in the sport, Leclerc has claimed nine Grand Prix victories.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also taking part-time drives in NASCAR's top series. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, competing from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris is a British Formula One driver currently competing for McLaren, where he secured the 2025 World Drivers' Championship. Throughout his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 13 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently competing for Haas in the championship.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Checo Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One and brings extensive experience from 15 seasons of competition. His notable achievements include finishing as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull, along with six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, where he has secured eight Grand Prix victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Jr. currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following prior stints in IMSA's LMP2 class. He competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to his current endurance racing commitments.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, holds a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver throughout 2021-2025, he transitioned to a backup position for the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen represents the Netherlands in Formula One while racing for Red Bull Racing. He has secured four consecutive world championship titles between 2021 and 2024, along with 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over his 12-season career.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve driver position with Cadillac. He continues his involvement with the sport in this supporting capacity.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team adopted the Alpine Racing name starting in 2021, replacing its previous Renault F1 identity while remaining Groupe Renault's factory operation. Operating under various sponsorship arrangements, the team represented Renault's motorsport presence in the championship until the manufacturer's withdrawal at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has entered Formula One competition through multiple team entities, with the current operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco branding.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP serves as the Formula One racing arm of the Italian luxury car manufacturer Ferrari. As the sport's most enduring and accomplished outfit, the team has participated continuously in the World Championship from its inception in 1950, earning the colloquial designation "the Prancing Horse" from its iconic emblem.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Gene Haas established this American-licensed Formula One team in 2014, with competitive operations commencing in 2016. Leadership transitioned when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role in early 2024, succeeding the team's founding principal Guenther Steiner.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering outfit established in 1970, Sauber initially built sports cars before transitioning to Formula One machinery as an independent constructor in 1993. The team competed across three decades, securing notable endurance racing honors including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours victory, before ceasing operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-running entrants. Audi acquired the organization and its operations in 2024 to serve as the foundation for its own Formula One program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited represents a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Technology Centre in Woking, Surrey. Operating as a subsidiary within the McLaren Group, the team competes under corporate sponsorship in the championship.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both constructor and power unit supplier, with the current iteration competing from a Brackley base under a German licence. Following an ownership restructure completed in January 2022, the team operates as a tripartite partnership between Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff, each holding equal stakes. The marque's racing heritage is epitomized by the "Silver Arrows" nomenclature, reflecting the iconic silver livery traditionally associated with German competitors.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's second constructors' entry into the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that entered the sport in 2024, operating as a sister team to Red Bull Racing under the ownership of Austrian conglomerate Red Bull GmbH. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Red Bull's expansion into operating two separate Formula One entities.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by the Red Bull conglomerate since its 2005 inception. The squad achieved notable stability under longtime team principal Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, with Laurent Mekies assuming leadership of the operation.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering Limited, the British team competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, was established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Operating from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters, the outfit has functioned as both team and chassis constructor throughout its Formula One tenure.
